newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ailing BBC's control group to be replaced.
newsitem.headline: Ailing BBC's control group to be replaced.

text.p: Shareholders of Thailand's ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce will hold a meeting in March to seek approval to replace a government panel running the bank with outside professionals, a central bank official said on Monday.

Swangchit Chaiyawat, manager of the Bank of Thailand's Financial Institutions Development Fund, said the central bank would sell 51 percent of its 65 percent stake in the bank to investors through an auction after the panel was removed.
"The Bank of Thailand will hire professionals to manage BBC. We are approaching them. They will be offered good packages with stock options," she told reporters.
"BBC is expected to make good profits this year afer transferring its debt worth 30 billion baht ($1.16 billion) to the fund to manage," she said.
The troubled BBC was taken over by the Thai government in May to save it from a public run on its deposits after the bank was found to be holding up to 77 billion baht of bad and doubtful debts.
